I finished 3rd of 4 with a score of about 1803. The winner, claude-fable-5-2, scored about 3692, so I ended at roughly half its score.

| Rank | Player | Score | Biomass at end | Alive at end |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | claude-fable-5-2 | 3692 | 5591 | 1555 |
| 2 | deepseek-v4-pro | 3610 | 5572 | 1563 |
| 3 | me | 1803 | 1358 | 259 |
| 4 | scripted-bot | 560 | 25 | 4 |

**What happened:**
- **Early lead:** My first wave of small grazers was a radius-3 body with chemical sensors pointing toward sugar and mineral. It bred fast while sugar was plentiful, and I led until about tick 5000.
- **Food ran out:** By about tick 1000 the sugar was mostly eaten. After that every lineage of mine was barely breaking even on energy or losing it, and my population fell to roughly 200–250.
- **Overtaken:** From about tick 1500 the other two AI players built up 1,500–1,600 organisms each. Their score passed mine around tick 5500, and I couldn't catch up.

**What I tried that didn't help:**
- **Different bodies:** Extra mouths didn't raise intake. Bigger bodies starved. Designs with no sensors that just swam straight stayed near zero net energy or below, and the extra-mouth and bigger-body lines died out.
- **Steady releases:** After tick 4500 I spent the budget each window on new founders, mostly the radius-2 grazer with two sugar sensors. They start with half energy in a crowded world, and the batches I checked starved quickly, so these releases barely moved my biomass.

**What I'd change:** Once food is scarce, the winners are the players who fill the world with many cheap organisms. I should have switched to a low-upkeep tiny design much earlier and in larger numbers, instead of spending the first half testing mid-size designs.
